newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Beach Pete says Q2 production, sales down.
newsitem.headline: Beach Pete says Q2 production, sales down.

text.p: Beach Petroleum NL said on Wednesday its Australian crude oil production, sales and revenue for the second quarter fell in Australia on the year-earlier level but rose for the smaller-scale United States operations.

In its quarterly report, Beach said its share of crude oil production in Australia from the onshore Naccowlah and Bodalla Block PLs 31, 32 and 47 was 66,781 barrels, down from 82,752 barrels in the 1996 quarter.
U.S. production for the quarter was 16,167 barrels, up from 13,144 barrels, due to the first contributions from new Mississippi Chat wells, it said.
Beach said its total oil sales in Australia for the quarter were 63,239 barrels, down on the year-earlier sales of 84,354 barrels, with sales in the U.S. up to 15,630 barrels from 13,144.

Beach's share of proceeds from the sale of hydrocarbons in Australia for the quarter was A$1.74 million, down from A$2.24 million in the same 1996 quarter, with sales in the U.S. up to A$432,000 from A$344,000.

Beach said a seismic survey was planned for July-August 1997 at the Taipan and Geiger prospects in the onshore Eromanga Basin permit ATP 548P of southwest Queensland, north-east of the Inland Oilfield, to define the best crestal location for drilling exploration wells.
